subject: Customer testimonial / reference request — timing & alternate contact
messages:
From: Samantha Lee <samantha@scalegrid.io>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick reference ask for procurement packet

Hi Rishi,

Hope you’re well. We’re in final procurement for a pilot and our legal/procurement team has asked for a short customer reference from an existing Redwood customer that uses the Dedicated offering. Ideally a 15–20 minute call with a customer contact who can confirm data isolation and general latency experience.

Timing is tight — procurement needs something before Apr 6. If a live call is hard, a one-paragraph written reference (signed) would also work.

If there are any customers who prefer not to be contacted, no problem — we’re happy with an anonymized case blurb instead. Can you let me know if Redwood can provide a contact this window and any constraints?

Thanks,
Samantha
Samantha Lee
Sr. Technical Program Manager — ScaleGrid
procurement@scalegrid.io

Attachment: RFQ_Checklist.pdf (attachment stub)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha@scalegrid.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Mar 2026 12:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick reference ask for procurement packet

Samantha —

Thanks for the note and congrats getting to procurement. I want to be transparent: several of our Dedicated customers have hit what we call ‘reference fatigue’ this quarter (we typically cap outreach to one interview per customer per quarter). That means a live 15–20 minute call for the Apr 6 window is unlikely from the contacts we currently have permission to surface.

Two options that would meet procurement needs quickly:
- I can provide a short, signed one-paragraph customer quote from one of our customers who has already approved written references. I can turn that around in 48 hours if that works for you.
- Alternatively, we can offer a substitute named customer for a short call, but I’ll need to confirm permission; that usually takes 2–5 business days.

If neither works and timing is absolute, we can supply an anonymized case blurb (redacted org and metrics) plus a short technical attestation from our product team about isolation and latency guarantees.

I’ve attached our customer_reference_form.pdf that shows the types of permissions customers typically grant — if you can tell me which of the three options you prefer, I’ll escalate accordingly.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Phone: (415) 555-0123

Attachment: customer_reference_form.pdf (attachment stub)

Hi all — copying in as Rishi & Marissa flagged the rotation concern. Approve outreach to Acme Retail for a single 15–20 minute procurement call this quarter. Marissa, please use the rotation sheet and flag this outreach as an exception in the "Notes" column if Acme agrees.

A few guardrails:
- If Acme says no, do not repeatedly ping them; move to the written quote option and provide procurement the signed paragraph.
- If Acme requires an NDA before speaking, route to Legal; we should not slow procurement for standard NDA reviews — we’ll prioritize a lightweight mutual NDA if needed.
- Offer ScaleGrid a one-paragraph signed quote immediately if there is any delay in customer permission. That keeps the procurement timeline moving.

As a goodwill gesture, I’m ok with applying a one-time 10% pilot credit to move this forward if needed (coordinate with Finance/CS). Marissa, if you get a yes from Laura please cc me and I’ll approve the credit and ensure it’s recorded on the opportunity.

Thanks — Lauren
